title: Chapter 28
content:
Jakyeong peeked over the top of the stone wall. The courtyard was deserted.

He had slipped past the surveillance cameras' blind spots until he reached the base of the perimeter, but scaling the wall and landing inside without making a sound was the real challenge. Gathering his momentum, he cleared the coping and dropped lightly onto the lawn.

A low, guttural growl vibrated through the dark.

Jakyeong froze. He lifted his gaze by fractions—only to find two pale eyes reflecting the moonlight. Baring rows of glistening fangs while thick saliva dripped from its jaws, the beast standing before him was Kang Il-hyun’s German Shepherd—the very animal sent away to behavioral camp for tearing a man apart.

Jakyeong took a slow, agonizing step backward. His spine hit the perimeter wall.

He shifted his weight laterally, searching for an escape angle, but the hound lunged with terrifying speed. Jakyeong took off in a full sprint along the brickwork, the dog’s frantic, booming barks shattering the night air.

"Ah, fuck me!"

Even a man who could run a hundred meters in eleven flat stood zero chance against an attack dog closing the gap at thirty-five miles per hour. He cut hard to the left, trying to juke the beast, but the maneuver did nothing. The distance evaporated in seconds. Just as the jaws snapped an inch from his tailbone—

A sharp, piercing whistle cut through the darkness.

The hound veered off instantly, trotting obediently toward the estate's main doors. Jakyeong bent double, hands braced against his knees, heaving for breath. Nausea churned in his gut, his heart pounding violently against his ribs. They say dogs take after their owners... this vicious brute is the spitting image of Kang Il-hyun.

Dragging his posture upright, he saw Il-hyun walking leisurely toward him through the shadows. A security handler emerged from the side path, clipping a lead to the dog's collar before leading it away.

"Are you alright?"

Jakyeong pushed his horn-rimmed frames up the bridge of his nose and nodded meekly.

"What are you doing out here at this hour?"

Drawing a deep breath to steady his racing pulse, Jakyeong swallowed the dry lump in his throat. He’d been racking his brain for a way to slip back into the house unnoticed, but this encounter handed him the perfect cover story.

"I felt suffocated in bed... so I came out for some fresh air. Then the dog came out of nowhere..."

Il-hyun’s eyes swept slowly down Jakyeong’s frame, taking in the rumpled clothes and damp skin. "How is your body?"

Jakyeong began to nod, then seized the opening to launch into a violent, racking coughing fit. Covering his mouth, he hacked as if his lungs were collapsing.

Il-hyun’s brows furrowed in immediate concern. "You look like you belong in an emergency room."

"I'm fine..." Jakyeong wheezed, pitching his voice into a trembling rasp. "Sprinting just now... made it flare up..."

As the coughing continued without pause, Il-hyun subtly took a half-step back. Look at that. Fearless when facing down assassins, but terrified of catching a common cold.

Jakyeong capitalized on the opening, doubling down on the performance until he was practically dry-heaving into his palm.

Il-hyun’s expression hardened. "Let's get you inside. I'll have a doctor summoned."

"My lungs are naturally weak... I just need to lie down and sleep it off. Going outside was a terrible mistake."

Jakyeong took the lead, with Il-hyun trailing silently behind. In a twisted way, the dog's ambush had been a blessing in disguise; otherwise, he might have spent the entire night shivering on the lawn.

The moment they crossed the threshold into the foyer, the housekeeper rushed over, her face lined with worry.

"Heavens, going outside in the damp air when you have a fever! Go straight upstairs, Young Master. I'll brew a pot of warm herbal tea."

"Please don't trouble yourself, ma'am... I'm so sorry for worrying everyone. Please get some rest."

Offering a polite bow to both Il-hyun and the housekeeper, Jakyeong retreated up the central staircase.

Positioning his body to shield the second-floor hallway camera, he slipped his lock-pick set from his seam, worked the pins for two seconds, and popped the bedroom deadbolt. He slipped inside, locked the door, and collapsed flat across the mattress.

"Ugh... I'm exhausted."

He lay sprawled like a corpse, staring up at the plaster ceiling, when two soft knocks sounded at the door.

Didn't I just tell the housekeeper to skip the tea?

Before he could pull himself up, the door swung open, and Kang Il-hyun stepped inside.

Jakyeong’s eyes narrowed into sharp slits. In all the time he’d stayed in this wing, Il-hyun had never once breached his private bedroom.

Setting a steaming porcelain mug onto the nightstand, Il-hyun casually took a seat on the edge of the mattress. "Drink this. It will soothe the cough."

Jakyeong stared at the indentation the man made on the bed. You brought the tea, now get out. Why are you sitting there?

"Go on. Drink it down."

"Thank you..."

Jakyeong picked up the mug and brought the rim to his lips. Out of the corner of his eye, he noted that Il-hyun showed zero intention of leaving, watching him with unwavering intensity.

The tea was punishingly bitter, carrying an earthy, medicinal stench that made his stomach turn. He managed half the cup before pulling a face, unable to force down another drop.

Il-hyun reached into his pocket, produced a lollipop, peeled back the plastic wrapper, and held it out. "Here."

Jakyeong reached out to take the stick, but Il-hyun pulled his hand back, parting his own lips in an exaggerated Ah.

Swallowing his pride, Jakyeong parted his lips. The sweet slipped past his teeth, coating his tongue in an instant rush of sugary strawberry syrup.

"Finish the tea," Il-hyun coaxed smoothly. "It doesn't just suppress the cough—it calms the nervous system."

Resigned, Jakyeong choked down the remaining bitter liquid, then popped the lollipop back into his mouth. As he rolled the candy against the roof of his mouth to chase away the medicinal aftertaste, he realized Il-hyun was leaning in close.

Jakyeong pulled the candy from his lips, his expression stiffening. "Is... is something wrong?"

Il-hyun closed his eyes slightly, drawing a slow, deliberate breath through his nose.

Jakyeong froze.

"Your soap smells different."

Jakyeong’s stomach dropped. He’d showered at Wang Ryun's garage using industrial hand soap, and this bastard had picked up the scent profile instantly. He really is a bloodhound.

Forcing an innocent smile, Jakyeong stammered out an excuse: "The house soap was irritating my skin, so I switched to a travel bar I brought from Hong Kong."

"Is that so?"

Il-hyun remained leaned in, hovering bare inches away. The tension in the bedroom turned suffocating. Jakyeong couldn't tell if the man was studying his face or staring at the wet sheen on his lips, but the slow, predatory sweep of those dark irises set every internal alarm ringing.

"Director Kang... I'm really quite drained. I think I should sleep now..."

"Put it back in."

"Pardon?"

"The lollipop. Put it back in your mouth."

What kind of sick game is this now?

Jakyeong popped the candy back between his teeth with a flat, deadpan expression.

"Not like that. Suck on it like you were doing a moment ago."

You absolute son of a bitch.

Suppressing the urge to drive the plastic stick through the man's eyeball, Jakyeong rolled his tongue over the candy, dissolving the sugar. Seeing his instructions obeyed, the corner of Il-hyun's mouth curled into an amused smile.

If I lick it, he'll probably lose his mind completely.

Driven by a spiteful urge to see how far the man would push, Jakyeong extended his tongue, slowly lapping at the glossy red surface.

Sure enough, a dark, thoroughly delighted chuckle rumbled in Il-hyun's chest.

"Look at you... Where on earth did you learn such filthy habits?"

Jakyeong scowled, popping the candy entirely back into his cheek.

When Il-hyun finally pushed himself up from the mattress, Jakyeong prepared to let out a sigh of relief—until the man paused at the threshold.

"I'll be counting on you later."

"For... what?"

"You know."

Il-hyun delivered a slow, deliberate wink.

A violent shudder raced down Jakyeong's spine, nearly causing him to drop the candy from his mouth. Did that pit-viper just wink at me?

Watching Jakyeong’s expression curdle into pure disgust, Il-hyun offered a warm, parting smile.

"I'll take my leave. The cameras have been completely removed, so feel free to strip down completely when you sleep."

"..."

"Sweet dreams."

The moment the heavy door clicked shut, Jakyeong spat the lollipop directly into the empty teacup and shot up from the bed.

The parting comment about sleeping naked was too suspicious to ignore. He swept the room from top to bottom, checking every vent and molding. Fortunately, there were no secondary bugs installed, but the lingering paranoia ensured he kept his briefs firmly on before getting under the covers.

[Clean work.]

Wang Han’s voice came through the encrypted receiver. He had already spoken with Wang Ryun and received the full debrief. Jakyeong had expected a lecture on taking unnecessary tactical risks, but his handler simply offered quiet validation instead. Wang Han understood the ghosts driving Jakyeong’s actions.

[Also, Dmitri finally checked in.]

Jakyeong stopped mid-stride toward the bed, his posture locking tight. "Who is it?"

[Kang Hoon.]

When Jakyeong didn't respond, Wang Han repeated the name with heavy emphasis.

[Did you hear me? Kang Hoon. Kang Il-hyun’s biological father.]

Jakyeong stood motionless. The image of the old patriarch at the family dinner flashed through his mind. The man possessed a terrifying, domineering aura, but he hadn't seemed like a father actively plotting to put a bullet through his favorite son's chest. In fact, if anything, he’d appeared to favor Il-hyun above the rest.

"Are you certain?"

[Positive. But do you want to guess who actually finalized the contract through the broker?]

"Who...?"

[Jang Myeong. You know the name, don't you?]

Jang Yi-an’s grandfather.

The revelation hit like a physical blow. Jakyeong had wondered what kind of heavyweight had enough pull to manipulate the Hong Kong Triad patriarch—only to find out it was the patriarch himself.

[According to Dmitri, the leadership in Hong Kong is split between those backing Kang Il-hyun and those opposing him. Jang Myeong had remained neutral until recently, but flipped his stance. The word is he finds Il-hyun’s aggressive expansion too volatile for long-term business... though Chairman Kang’s influence almost certainly nudged the needle.]

"Then who does Chairman Kang want on the throne?"

[Kang Tae-han.]

That sniveling, narrow-eyed coward. Tae-han lacked the intellect, the spine, and the presence required to run a global conglomerate.

[The Chairman’s health took a sharp dive last year, which put Il-hyun at the front of the succession race. To make matters worse for the old man, several key institutional shareholders who used to back Tae-han have begun jumping ship to Il-hyun's camp. Kang Hoon is staring down a future where his second son takes everything. But the old tiger has zero intention of surrendering power. His play is simple: install the spineless Tae-han as a puppet CEO while he continues pulling the strings from the shadows.]

Jakyeong remained silent. Does Kang Il-hyun have any idea his own father is orchestrating his execution?

[Jakyeong.]

"Yeah."

[We do the job we're paid to do. Nothing more, nothing less.]

"I know. Don't worry. I'll finish this cleanly."

Ending the call, Jakyeong walked over to the glass wall and looked out over the estate. Finding out the client's identity was supposed to provide operational clarity, but it had only muddied the waters. It would have been simpler if Il-hyun had placed the hit on himself after all...

He shook the absurd thought from his head. Contract wet-work didn't leave room for philosophical dilemmas; you take the cash, you pull the trigger, and you move on.

Hanging in the center of the night sky, the full moon glowed with an eerie, deep crimson hue—as if it were poised to bleed over the horizon at any moment.

Jakyeong drew the heavy blackout blinds shut, sealing the room in darkness, and dropped onto the mattress.

The parameters of the mission hadn't changed in the slightest. When the inauguration date arrived, he would put a round through Kang Il-hyun’s heart and board the first flight out of the country.

It was that simple.
